name: Lomita City Council Special Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES OF THE
  LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL MEETING
  THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 24, 2022

PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER N-08.21 ISSUED BY GOVERNOR NEWSOM AND
A8361, THE PUBLIC AND COUNCIL PARTICIPATED IN THIS MEETING IN PERSON AND VIA
ZOOM.

,|
  OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order
  The special meeting of the Lomita Ci$ Council was called to order by Mayor Segawa at
  3:03 p.m. on Thursday, February 24,2022.

  b. Roll Call
  PRESENT: Council Members Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa (all participated in-person)

  $!NT: None
  STAFF PRESENT: City Manager Smoot, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney
  Rusin, Administrative Services Director Kamada, and Public Works Director Dillon (in-person)

  Recreation Manager Kelley, Management Analyst Vida, Management Assistant Adamzadeh,
  Management Analyst Hemandez, Administrative Analyst lbarra, Administrative Clerk lll Paz,
  Recreation Supervisor Edwards, Community and Ec,onomic Development Director Kapovich,
  and City Clerk Gregory (participated via Zoom)

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  There were no requests from the public to speak during oral communications.

  RECESS FOR CLOSED SESSION

  The Council recessed to closed session at 3:05 p.m

3  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL_ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to $ 5a956.9(d)(2): One matter
  Letter received January 18,2022, from Kevin Shenkman regarding threat of litigation under
  California Voting Rights Act of 2001.

February 24,2022

  RECONVENE FOROPEN SESSION

  The Council reconvened to open session at 4:28 p.m.

4. CLOSEO SESSION REPORT-CITYATTORNEY
  City Attorney Rusin announced that the City Council met in closed session at 3:05 p.m. to
  discuss lhe item on the posted agenda, all members of the City Council were present, and
  there was no reportable action taken.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS

5. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF FISCAL YEAR2021-2022 MID-YEAR BUOGET
  AMENDMENTS

  REGOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the recommendations contained in Attachment No. 1
  and direct staff to make necessary expenditure and revenue budget adjustments to implement
  the recommendations.

  City Manager Smoot presented the staff report as per the agenda material. He reviewed the
  2021 Cily Goals as established by the City Council:

  o Continue to lmprove Streets and Water Lines
  o Continue to lmprove Water Quality - Complete Phase I and Evaluate Phase ll
  . Enhance Economic Development in Downtown and PCH
  . Maintain and Enhance Public Safety Efforts, Traffic Enforcement and Community
  lnvolvement
  o Clarify Housing Development and Design Standards
  . Continue Legislative Advocacy Efforts and Regional lnfluence and Engagement
  . Resilience and Learning from the Pandemic to Build a City that can withstand a Crisis
  . Develop a Financing Plan and Kickoff General Plan Update
  City Manager Smoot outlined the highlighted projects and goals set for the City
  Manager's Department, which include upgrades to broadband and improvements to City
  Council Chambers, among other projects.

  City Manager Smoot introduced Los Angeles County Building Official Michael Dorta (via
  Zoom) who outlined building permits issued since 2019.

  City Manager Smoot outlined Community and Economic Development Department
  highlighted projects and goals, which include increased and enhanced code enforcement and
  SB9 and ADU ordinance updates.

  City Manager Smoot outlined Facilities and Recreation's highlighted projects and goals, which
  include the Contract Cities Annual Municipal Seminar and the Navy baseball fields agreement.

  After a brief discussion relative to the Navy baseball field, Council Member Gazeley made a
  motion, seconded by Council Member Waite to form an ad hoc committee to include Mayor
  Segawa and Council Member Waronek to work with slaff on the specifics of any agreement
  and potential funding sources for necessary work before City Council consideration.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Recreation Manager Kelley presented an update on City events, including Founders Day and
  the Lomita Mayor's Cup.

  It was the consensus of the Council to schedule the Lomita Mayor's Cup for fall, likely in
  September.

  City Manager Smoot outlined Public Works Department (Water, Field Ops, Engineering)
  highlighted projects and goals, which include the Water Master Plan and the 2021-22 Street
  Project (Zones C&F&G).

  Public Works Director Dillon presented a brief update on the G.A.C. upgrades at the Cypress
  Water Production Facility.

  City Manager Smoot outlined the highlighted projects and goals of the Administrative Services
  Department, which include updated financial policies and pension obligation bonds.

  Administrative Services Director Kamada presented brief updates on the City's efforts to
  consolidate certain online services and pension obligation bonds. She presented the mid-year
  Budget update as per the agenda material, noting the following:

  The city's general fund budget is $1 '1,446,567.
  All funds total $31 ,531,241 .
  The unassigned general fund balance as ofJune 30,202'l, was $5,123,26'1. The prior
  year unassigned general fund balance was $5,004,836. This represents an increase in
  the general fund balance of $118,425 for FY 202012021.
  As of June 30, 2021, the city's long-term debt was $5,995,000.

  There were no requests to speak on this item, therefore Mayor Segawa asked for a motion.

  Council Member Uphoff made a motion, seconded by Council Member Waronek to approve
  the recommended action.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  PUBLIC HEARING

6. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION
  USER FEES

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt the proposed Resolution No. 2022-07, approving User
  Fees for the City's Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations.

  Administrative Analyst lbarra presented the staff report as per the agenda material.

  Mayor Segawa opened the public hearing at 6:04 p.m. As there were no requests from the
  public to speak on this item, Mayor Segawa closed the public hearing at 6:04 p.m. and brought
  the item back to Council for further discussion or a motion.

  Council Member Gazeley made a motion, seconded by Council Member Uphoff to approve
  the recommended action.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Adopted the following titled resolution:

  RESOLUTION NO.2022.07 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND ADOPTING ELECTRIC VEHICLE (EV)
  CHARGING STATION USER FEES

7. ADJOURNMENT
  There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Segawa adjourned the meeting, at
  6:06 p.m.
